candidates.title: store() with SHARING_NONE or SHARING_CONFIG copies the source directory's un-rebuilt .dht/.dpt files, so an O1 rebuild done with clear_hash_tree is lost and the operator's own synced snapshot reloads with the foreign template's stale root hash
candidates.component: Emulator core: storing machines (machine::store, src/machine.cpp) together with the O1 rebuild (machine_runtime_config.clear_hash_tree / machine::clear_hash_tree -> hash_tree::clear); reachable from C cm_store, Lua machine:store(dir, SHARING_NONE|SHARING_CONFIG), JSON-RPC machine.store and the CLI --store=<dir>,sharing:none|config
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md table: 'storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines'). If the sharing modes none/config are judged off the honest operator's path, the machine-API reading applies (give both ratings).
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp machine::store, lines 453-481: for an unshared range (sharing==none, or sharing==config with c.shared==false, the value every stored config.json written with the default sharing carries) it runs os::copy_file(c.data_filename, ...) and, when c.dht_filename and c.dpt_filename are set, os::copy_file(c.dht_filename, dht_filename) and os::copy_file(c.dpt_filename, dpt_filename). For a loaded machine, c.* are the files of the loaded directory (machine_config::load -> adjust_ar_backing_store_config). src/machine.hpp:466 clear_hash_tree() -> src/hash-tree.cpp:744 hash_tree::clear() only clears the in-memory dense trees, dirty-page trees, sparse nodes and page cache; for an unshared load those are MAP_PRIVATE mappings (src/dense-hash-tree.hpp:63, src/dirty-page-tree.hpp:102 with shared=false), so the files on disk keep the foreign cached data. Lines 513-516 write blank sht/phtc, and update_sparse_tree (hash-tree.cpp:566-578) resyncs the sparse tree from the copied dense roots, so the copied dht/dpt pair alone decides the root hash on reload.
candidates.description: O1 adoption is done by loading the foreign stored machine with clear_hash_tree=true (or calling clear_hash_tree), which rebuilds the cached hash tree in memory. For an unshared load the rebuild never reaches the files. store(dir, SHARING_NONE) and store(dir, SHARING_CONFIG) (for ranges whose config.json says shared=false, which is how cartesi-machine --store and machine:store write them) do not serialize the in-memory trees: they copy the ORIGINAL backing files, and copy the original .dht and .dpt files next to them as a trusted pair. The new directory therefore carries the foreign template's un-rebuilt dense hash trees and clean dirty-page marks. It was written by the operator's own process and, after sync_stored, is a directory O2 guarantees. Reloading it without clear_hash_tree (allowed by R1/O2 for the operator's own snapshot) yields the foreign cached root hash instead of the content hash, verify_hash_tree fails, and every later root hash computed from it (after running, delivering, collecting) is wrong because untouched pages keep their stale dense-tree hashes. The rollback semantics of these modes are documented ('copies backing stores from the initial machine state'), but copying the initial cached trees after the operator explicitly rebuilt them defeats the rebuild; the stored config.json does not record that the trees must be rebuilt (unlike mark_pages_dirty, which adjust_backing_stores preserves).
candidates.trigger: Whoever supplies the template (an application developer or any party distributing a stored machine) ships a directory whose contents match the on-chain commitment but whose .dht/.dpt files describe other contents. The honest operator follows O1 (loads with clear_hash_tree, checks the root hash: it matches), then stores the adopted machine with sharing none or config (e.g. cartesi-machine --load=<template> --clear-hash-tree --store=<mine>,sharing:config, or cm_store(m, dir, CM_SHARING_CONFIG)), syncs it, and later reloads its own snapshot without rebuilding.
candidates.reachability: No guest action is needed; the stale data comes from the adopted directory, which meets every valid-template condition (its content hash after the rebuild equals the commitment). Any template whose cached data is stale qualifies, including an honest one whose files were edited or regenerated without updating the cache. The store modes are public, documented API modes of cm_store/Lua/JSON-RPC/CLI. The PRT player in doc/recipes stores with the default SHARING_ALL and is not affected; whether a production node uses none/config is unknown.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The exclusion 'Defects that need the cached hash-tree data of a stored machine the operator did not produce to survive its adoption without a rebuild (O1)' does not apply: the operator performs the rebuild exactly as O1 requires ('rebuilds the cached hash-tree data from the contents when loading it, and only then compares the root hash'); the emulator then re-emits the pre-rebuild data. Section 5: 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too ... A defect that defeats the rebuild itself, or that damages a directory while O2 guarantees it, is not excused by them.' The reloaded directory is O2-guaranteed ('synced after the last change to its contents' and never used with sharing). 2 Role: storing machines is Honest operator per AUDIT.md ('storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines'). 3 High/Medium cases: if store with sharing none/config is off the honest operator's path, this is Medium: 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree, the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9).' 4 Critical: on the honest operator's path ('Storing and reloading the machine', 'Obtaining its valid template ... rebuilding its cached hash-tree data (O1)') it violates R9 ('The content hash must equal the root of the actual contents. This applies to every cached, incremental, or persisted hash ... and every snapshot the emulator itself writes' where that means 'a directory that O2 guarantees') and R1's clause on cached data ('On the honest operator's path, it was either written by the operator's own process into a directory that O2 guarantees, or rebuilt from the contents on adoption (O1). This rule applies to it') -> Critical (completeness failure: 'The honest operator computes a wrong hash'). 5 n/a. Which reading holds depends on whether a production validator stores adopted templates with sharing none/config.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical if storing with sharing none/config is on the honest operator's path; Medium otherwise
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure: after a correct O1 adoption, the operator's own guaranteed snapshot reports a root hash chosen by whoever wrote the template's cache files, and every claim and proof built from it is wrong, so the honest claim is eliminated and a dishonest claim can win. The operator has no reason to rebuild again, since R1/O2 say its own synced snapshot is trusted.
candidates.evidence: Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFSTORED/scripts/storenone.lua on bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template/machine: populate the template's cache with a SHARING_ALL load, change 64 bytes of RAM in the .bin behind the cache's back (stale cache), load with clear_hash_tree=true (true hash != stale hash: rebuild works), store(mine, mode), sync_stored, reload mine without clear_hash_tree. Results: mode none -> reload==true false, reload==stale true, verify_hash_tree false ('page 0x80100000 (in RAM) is not marked dirty but is dirty', 'RAM dense hash tree root does not match sparse node hash'); mode config -> same, and after running 1000 mcycles the no-rebuild and rebuild hashes still differ; mode all -> reload==true true (control).
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: copy a harness stored machine, populate its cache (SHARING_ALL load + get_root_hash), patch bytes of a RAM page in the .bin file, load it with {clear_hash_tree=true} and record H; for each of SHARING_NONE and SHARING_CONFIG store it to a fresh directory, sync_stored, reload without clear_hash_tree and assert get_root_hash()==H and verify_hash_tree()==true (fails now, passes once store writes rebuilt or blank trees, or forces mark_pages_dirty, when the in-memory trees were cleared or no longer correspond to the source files).

candidates.title: clone_stored decides hard link versus reflink from the template's file mode bits and keeps short backing files, so a valid template distributed read-only or with trailing zeros trimmed cannot be cloned and loaded with sharing (PRT stored player and CLI clone: fail)
candidates.component: Emulator core: cloning and loading stored machines (machine::clone_stored, os::clone_file, os::mapped_memory); callers: PRT stored player (doc/recipes/prt.lua new_stored_player, store_first_epoch_checkpoint), CLI --load=<dir>,clone:<src> (default sharing all)
candidates.role: Honest operator (cloning/loading machines); the PRT player and CLI are Support
candidates.location: src/os-filesystem.cpp clone_file lines 577-622 (read_only = no write bit in st_mode -> hardlink_file, else reflink_file, fallback copy_file which preserves the mode); src/machine.cpp clone_stored 526-577 (clones every data/dht/dpt/sht/phtc file as is, no length normalization); src/os-mapped-memory.cpp 59-69 check_shared_write_backing_file (refuses read-only or nlink>1 files for shared write) and 164-175 (shared mapping refuses a backing file shorter than the range); doc/recipes/prt.lua 3209-3216 (clone template, then new_stored_machine with SHARING_ALL + clear_hash_tree).
candidates.description: File modes, link counts and backing-file lengths are outside the hashed state. A template whose writable ranges' files (or cached hash-tree files) lack write permission bits, e.g. because it was packaged or protected read-only (tar/OCI layer, chmod -R a-w, read-only store), loads fine unshared and its rebuilt hash matches, but clone_stored hard-links every such file (or copies it keeping mode 0444 across filesystems), and any SHARING_ALL load of the clone then throws 'is read-only and cannot be shared for writing' (and 'has multiple hard links'). Likewise a template whose data file is shorter than its range (trailing zero pages trimmed: same contents, same hash, loads unshared through backing_gap) is cloned short and the shared load throws 'length ... does not match desired backing length'. clear_hash_tree cannot help because the load fails first. The clone is the documented way to adopt a template for on-disk operation (manual: '--load=<dir>,clone:<src>' with default sharing all; PRT stored player). Store(SHARING_ALL) of an unshared load would normalize both, so a workaround exists.
candidates.trigger: Template supplier (or the operator's own packaging) distributes a valid template whose files are read-only or trimmed; the operator adopts it with clone_stored + shared load.
candidates.reachability: Any valid template; no guest action. Reproduced with the harness baremetal template.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The snapshot meets every valid-template condition (unshared load with clear_hash_tree gives the reference hash), and section 8 says 'Once a snapshot meets them, nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory.' Not excluded by O1 (the failure prevents the rebuild) or O2. 2 Role: clone/load are Honest operator; the player and CLI that break are Support. 3 High/Medium: no wrong hash, a loud failure; the closest listed case is Medium 'A persistence operation that fails loudly, without a wrong hash or damage to a directory that O2 guarantees, in an uncommon host setup that the manual documents', but a read-only template is not a documented host setup. 4 Critical reading: the honest operator's path includes 'Obtaining its valid template' and R4 'From any reachable state ... the honest operator can always compute the claim'; if clone + shared load is the operator's adoption path, a valid template that cannot be adopted is a completeness failure. Because store(SHARING_ALL) offers a working path and the defect shows in the support player/CLI, I rate it Medium (support defect that would be High/Critical in the honest-operator role), Low if triage holds that the emulator's own behavior is as documented ('Read-only backing files are hard-linked').
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Low if the documented hard-link behavior is accepted and only support components are affected)
candidates.threat_to_goal: The honest operator (stored PRT player, or any node adopting templates by clone + sharing) fails to start on a valid template because of attributes outside the hashed state; until an operator works around it, it cannot defend its claim (completeness).
candidates.evidence: scripts/ro.lua and scripts/short.lua in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFSTORED/ on the harness baremetal template: (A) chmod a-w on all files: unshared load with clear_hash_tree gives the reference hash; clone_stored creates nlink=2 hard links; SHARING_ALL load of the clone fails 'backing file .../0000000000000000-8000.bin is read-only and cannot be shared for writing when initializing shadow state'; store(SHARING_ALL) of the unshared load then loads shared fine. (B) RAM .bin truncated to 2367488 bytes (last nonzero byte at 2363740): unshared hash equal to reference; shared load of the clone fails 'length (2367488) does not match desired backing length (67108864)'. (C) only hash_tree.phtc read-only: shared load of the clone fails 'hash_tree.phtc is read-only'.
candidates.test_idea: Copy a harness template, chmod a-w its files (and separately truncate its RAM .bin to the last nonzero page); assert the unshared clear_hash_tree load gives the reference hash, then clone_stored and assert that load(clone, {clear_hash_tree=true}, SHARING_ALL) succeeds with the same hash (fails now).

not_covered: Did not run the PRT player (stored mode) end to end with a read-only or trimmed template, nor the player-restart harness; candidate 2's player impact is inferred from prt.lua lines 3209-3216 plus the emulator-level reproduction.

JSON-RPC server paths (machine.load/store/clone_stored over cartesi-jsonrpc-machine, fork_server, rebind) were only read for parameter defaults (load defaults to sharing none, store requires sharing); not exercised with crafted directories.

Deliberately not re-reported (already listed in context): malformed/missing cached files throwing before the rebuild (R1-O1-1), config.json phtc_size (R1-O1-2), player's template check without rebuild (R1-O1-3), hash function vs cached tree (R1-R11-3).

Huge or deeply padded config.json (os::read_file allocates st_size bytes; dtb.bootargs and other unhashed strings are carried into every later store/clone): considered, judged weak (a dense multi-GB file, loading cost linear in it) and not reported.

Symlinks/FIFOs/device files named as backing files inside an adopted directory (clone_file and mapped_memory follow symlinks; open of a FIFO would block): considered only; such directories arguably fail the valid-template conditions.
replace_memory_range with replacement backing stores that bring their own .dht/.dpt (caller-supplied cache data) and store(SHARING_NONE) after replace_memory_range: read, not tested.

Page-hash-tree cache (phtc) persisted entries with an 'initialized' tag across store(SHARING_ALL)/reload of operator-written directories, and m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages not being persisted: read only; found no stored-directory input that makes update() fail.
Reflink-capable filesystems (btrfs/XFS): the harness host is ext4, so reflink always fell back to copy; reflink-specific behavior (shared extents, FICLONE partial failures) not tested.
Windows/macOS paths of clone/copy/sync (clonefile, FlushFileBuffers), and host umask effects on files the emulator creates (S_CREATE_FILE & ~umask making later shared loads refuse).
cartesi-machine CLI combinations of --revert-mode=stored with --clear-hash-tree=once/always and clone:/sharing:config beyond reading.

The PRT player's own epoch-directory files (state.json, inputs/, forests/, epoch.json, outputs-frontier.json written into the checkpoint's stored-machine directory) were read only for name handling, not fuzzed.
